text: So before the 1950s, it was really slow and expensive to move things across the ocean. Things came in sacks and barrels and crates and individual people would lift them, loading and unloading. Ships would stay in port longer than they were at sea. Malcolm McLean was a trucking magnate from North Carolina, and he was very frustrated with the efficiency of docks, and he had an idea. He converted a tanker ship into a container ship. It was called Ideal X. And it carried 58 containers from New Jersey to Texas. It took hours to load rather than days. And it reduced the cost per ton dramatically. And then he standardized the container size so that any truck, crane, train or ship could handle the same container. And the international standards came in in the 1960s, of 20 feet and 40 feet in length. And they had the corner fittings that could lock in securely. By the 1970s, container ships were no longer converted tankers, they were purpose-built. They could carry thousands of containers. And it completely transformed shipping. Port cities were rebuilt around container cranes, container yards. The old port areas were ruined, became very cheap. The cost of freight went down dramatically. And the world could source and sell things globally. And it's just a steel box that you can put on top of another steel box, that transformed the 20th century profoundly.
